note: Phase 10 (External agent validation), added 2026-10-16 after the core roadmap (TB-001..TB-054) and before the optional extensions. Planned only: every task starts Not Started and nothing in it is implemented until TB-054 is Completed. The sealed core holdout (data/splits.json) is never used here: it has one confirmatory use, by TB-032. Source of the rows written into planning/TrustBench-AI_Plan.xlsx. Revised 2026-10-16 after review: TB-061 registers the split procedure and TB-062 applies it and freezes the manifests (resolves a circular dependency); TB-057/TB-058 add a native-integration mode in which the agent keeps its own independently implemented tool integration against a sandbox. Revised 2026-10-17: external agents also connect through the public live website and API (docs/live-service.md).

tasks.steps: Define selection criteria (developed independently of TrustBench, open-source licence permitting evaluation, tool or function calling, runs on free models or local Ollama, active maintenance, pinned release). Shortlist 3 candidates, score them against the criteria, pick one and pin the exact commit or release. Record why the others were rejected.
tasks.tools: Git, licence review, Ollama / NVIDIA / Gemini free tiers
tasks.acceptance: A selection record names the agent, its pinned version and licence, shows it was not written for TrustBench, and states that its core will not be modified beyond a documented adapter.
tasks.risk: No candidate supports tool calling on free models: fall back to a local model through Ollama, or document the gap and stop the phase before any claim.

tasks.task: Define the external-agent threat model and integration contract
tasks.steps: Map the external agent's trust boundaries: where prompts, tool outputs, memory and plugins enter. Decide which controls sit outside the agent (gateway, capability tokens, sandbox network policy) and which the agent cannot be trusted to enforce. Write the integration contract: tool names, argument schemas, error codes and trace fields the adapter must preserve.
tasks.inputs: TB-002 threat model; external agent architecture docs
tasks.acceptance: Contract and threat model reviewed against TB-002; every external entry point is classified as trusted or untrusted with the control that covers it, and any uncovered entry point is listed as out of scope.
tasks.risk: The agent has hidden tool paths (built-in browsing, shell, file access): disable them through configuration, or list them as uncovered and exclude them from claims.

tasks.task: Build the external-agent adapter (TrustBench tools and the agent's own tool integration)
tasks.steps: Mode A (controlled tools): expose the TrustBench tool services to the agent through its native tool interface (function tools or an MCP server), routed through the policy gateway. Mode B (native integration): keep at least one of the agent's own, independently implemented tool integrations (for example its SQL, HTTP-API or mail connector) unchanged, point it at a sandboxed local instance (database container or mock API server seeded with synthetic data, no real accounts), and interpose the gateway between that integration and its service without replacing the agent's tool environment. In both modes translate run configuration, model settings and step limits, and capture tool calls, final text and errors into the TrustBench trace schema. Keep the agent's own code unmodified. External agents are connected through the live website and API as well as locally: the run API reserves the agent field (external_mcp, langgraph_http, configs/live-service.yaml).
tasks.tools: Agent SDK or MCP, src/gateway, TypeScript or Python adapter, Docker (sandboxed database or mock API)
tasks.inputs: Integration contract (TB-056); gateway and tool services; the agent's native tool integration and a synthetic sandbox instance for it
tasks.acceptance: Mode A: adapter tests show every TrustBench tool callable from the agent and traces validating against the TB-004 schema. Mode B: at least one independently implemented native integration runs unchanged against its sandbox with every call passing through the gateway, which records an allow or deny decision per call; the sandbox holds synthetic data only. A diff proves no change to the agent's source or to the native integration's code. A connected external agent receives the same paired report through the website and trustbench remote.
tasks.risk: The agent's tool interface cannot carry capability tokens: hold tokens in the adapter process, never in prompts, and enforce at the gateway. The native integration cannot be interposed (in-process client, pinned TLS): use a network-level proxy in the sandbox, or record Mode B as not demonstrated and limit claims to Mode A.

tasks.task: Enforce tool authorization outside the agent
tasks.steps: Run the agent in a sandbox whose only route to tools is the gateway (network egress denied, raw tool service unreachable). Bind each episode to a capability token held outside the agent. Add bypass tests: direct calls to tool services, forged or replayed tokens, unlisted tools, argument smuggling and calls after cancellation. Repeat the bypass tests against the Mode B native integration: its client must reach the sandboxed service only through the gateway.
tasks.tools: Docker or a sandbox network policy, src/policy, pytest
tasks.inputs: TB-021 capability policy; TB-023 boundary tests
tasks.acceptance: Every bypass test is refused and audited in both adapter modes (TrustBench tools and the native integration); a positive control proves each test can detect a working bypass; no tool effect occurs without a gateway allow decision in the audit log.
tasks.risk: The agent framework makes network calls of its own (telemetry, model hub): allowlist only the model endpoint and record it.

tasks.task: Map tasks and fixtures to the external agent
tasks.steps: Deliver each benign task and attack fixture through the agent's native input (task prompt, documents as tool outputs). Keep fixtures, initial state and evaluators identical to the core benchmark; record any task the agent cannot express and why.
tasks.acceptance: Every development fixture either runs end to end with the unchanged evaluators or is listed with the reason it cannot; no holdout fixture is loaded (asserted by the runner).
tasks.risk: The agent rewrites or summarises tool outputs before acting, changing what an injection sees: record it as agent behaviour, not a fixture defect.

tasks.task: Run conformance and smoke tests on the external agent
tasks.steps: Run scripted (mock-model) conformance tests for the adapter, then a small live smoke run on the development split with both arms (agent alone, agent behind the gateway). Check traces, evaluator verdicts, spans and redaction end to end. Run the conformance and smoke checks through the live service as well.
tasks.tools: Playwright or pytest, scripts/run-arm-smoke.mjs pattern, free models
tasks.acceptance: Conformance suite passes; live smoke produces valid paired reports with complete evidence and no sensitive values in spans.
tasks.risk: Free-tier rate limits: pace requests and mark rate-limited runs invalid, never as results.

tasks.task: Pre-register the external validation protocol and split procedure
tasks.steps: Write an amendment before any external evaluation run: hypotheses, primary endpoints (unsafe committed-effect rate, benign utility), integration-overhead measures, adapter modes, repetitions, models, analysis and stopping rules. Register the split procedure, not the split: which fixture families are eligible (existing families never used in tuning, and families to be authored in TB-062), the seeded assignment rule to tuning or external validation, stratification, and the requirement that the sealed core holdout is excluded. Implement the procedure as a script and test it on placeholder family lists.
tasks.inputs: TB-006 protocol; experiment registry; inventory of existing fixture families and their tuning use
tasks.acceptance: Amendment committed and verified before the first external evaluation run; the split script is committed with tests showing it is deterministic for its seed, excludes the core holdout and every tuning-used family, and refuses to reassign a family once assigned.
tasks.risk: The procedure is changed after families are seen: any change needs a new amendment committed before TB-062 assigns families.

tasks.steps: Author attack families closer to deployment: injections inside long realistic documents, tool-output injection across several tools, multi-step and delayed instructions, data exfiltration through allowed tools, and attacks on the agent's own planning or memory features. Each family has an oracle, a benign twin and a positive control. Then apply the TB-061 split procedure to the new and eligible existing families, write data/external-splits.json, and freeze the attack and split manifests with content hashes before any defended evaluation run.
tasks.tools: data/ fixture builders, attack oracles, src/arms materialization
tasks.acceptance: Each family has a cited source or rationale, an oracle validated on scripted trajectories, a benign twin, and a split assigned by the registered TB-061 script; the split manifest is disjoint from the core holdout and the tuning families (checked by script) and its hash is committed before any defended run; positive controls succeed against the undefended agent.
tasks.risk: Attacks tuned to defeat or to favour the gateway: freeze them before any defended run and report their source. Too few families for a meaningful external split: author more before assignment, never after.

tasks.task: Test reliability and faults on the external agent
tasks.steps: Inject tool timeouts, 5xx errors, malformed and oversized outputs, slow responses and cancellations through the adapter; check the agent's recovery, the gateway's replay safety and that no write is duplicated. Measure how often runs end at runtime limits.
tasks.tools: TB-025 fault schedules, TB-026 durability, pytest
tasks.acceptance: Every fault class is exercised; no duplicate committed write; termination and recovery rates reported per fault class with intervals.
tasks.risk: The agent's own retry logic double-sends writes: rely on gateway idempotency keys and report the agent behaviour.

tasks.steps: Run the external agent alone and behind the gateway on the external validation split, identical tasks, seeds, schedules and model revision, within the free-tier budget. Keep invalid, rate-limited and missing runs visible.
tasks.tools: Batch runner, TB-028 schedules, free models
tasks.inputs: External validation split (data/external-splits.json, frozen in TB-062), frozen gateway configuration (configs/frozen/)
tasks.acceptance: Paired reports for every scheduled unit or a recorded reason for each missing one; the provider revision is recorded and constant, or the comparison is labelled invalid.
tasks.risk: Provider model changes mid-run: rerun both arms or label the comparison invalid.

tasks.task: Measure security, utility and integration overhead
tasks.steps: Compute the co-primary endpoints with cluster-bootstrap intervals, the false-block rate, latency and token overhead of the gateway path, and the integration cost (adapter size, agent configuration changes, unsupported features). Compare with the core results without pooling.
tasks.acceptance: Metrics recomputed from raw records by script; every number links to its runs; integration overhead reported in measured units.
tasks.risk: Small samples: report intervals and refrain from claims the data cannot support.

tasks.task: Report limitations and the integration guide
tasks.steps: Write what transferred and what did not, negative results, uncovered entry points, the agent behaviours that weakened or strengthened the controls, and a step-by-step guide for wrapping another agent. Add the external results to the review site. Publish the external-agent path on the live website: a visitor connects an agent (LangGraph or a customer agent) and gets the report.
tasks.acceptance: Limitations section lists every uncovered entry point and failed check; the guide is followed once on a clean checkout; claims stay within the measured scope. The live website guide is followed once with an external agent end to end.
tasks.risk: Overgeneralising from one external agent: state the single-agent scope in every claim.
